nodes.title: Area Under a Curve (Bounded by X-axis)
points: Area bounded by curve y = f(x), the X-axis, and ordinates x = a and x = b:
Formula: Area A = ∫_a^b y dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx.
Sign Convention: Area is always a positive scalar quantity. If curve lies BELOW the X-axis (y < 0), the integral is negative; take absolute value: Area = |∫_a^b y dx|.
If curve crosses the X-axis at x = c (a < c < b): Area = |∫_a^c y dx| + |∫_c^b y dx|.

nodes.title: Area Bounded by Y-axis
points: Area bounded by curve x = g(y), the Y-axis, and abscissae y = c and y = d:
Formula: Area A = ∫_c^d x dy = ∫_c^d g(y) dy.
If curve lies to the left of Y-axis (x < 0), take absolute value: Area = |∫_c^d x dy|.
Particularly convenient for horizontal parabolas x = y²/4a or curves naturally expressed as x = g(y).

nodes.title: Area Enclosed Between Two Curves
points: Area between upper curve y = f(x) and lower curve y = g(x) from x = a to x = b:
Formula: Area A = ∫_a^b [y_upper − y_lower] dx = ∫_a^b [f(x) − g(x)] dx.
Steps to solve area between curves:
1. Solve equations simultaneously to find points of intersection (giving integration limits a and b).
2. Sketch rough diagram to identify which curve is upper and which is lower.
3. Integrate the difference [y_upper − y_lower] from lower limit a to upper limit b.

nodes.title: Standard Geometric Curves: Circle & Ellipse
points: Area of Circle x² + y² = a²:
By symmetry, total area = 4 × (Area in 1st quadrant) = 4 ∫₀^a √(a² − x²) dx = 4 [(x/2)√(a²−x²) + (a²/2)sin⁻¹(x/a)]_0^a = 4(a²/2)(π/2) = π a².
Area of Ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1:
By symmetry, total area = 4 × ∫₀^a (b/a) √(a² − x²) dx = 4(b/a) (πa²/4) = π a b.
Standard 4-mark Board derivation question!

formulas.label: Area of ellipse derivation
formulas.expr: A = 4 (b/a) ∫₀^a √(a² − x²) dx = π a b

nodes.title: Parabola and Line Enclosed Area
points: Area bounded by parabola y² = 4ax and line y = mx:
Intersection points: Put y = mx ⟹ (mx)² = 4ax ⟹ x = 0, x = 4a/m².
Area A = ∫₀^(4a/m²) [2√(ax) − mx] dx = (8/3)(a² / m³).
Area bounded by parabola y² = 4ax and its Latus Rectum x = a:

nodes.title: Area Between Two Intersecting Parabolas
points: Area enclosed between y² = 4ax and x² = 4by:
Points of intersection: (0, 0) and (4 a^(1/3) b^(2/3), ...).
Formula: Area = (16 / 3) a b.
Special Case: Area between y² = 4ax and x² = 4ay:
Formula: Area = (16 / 3) a².
Example: Area between y² = 4x and x² = 4y is (16/3)(1)² = 16/3 sq. units.

nodes.title: Trigonometric & Modulus Curve Areas
points: One Arch of Sine Wave: Area bounded by y = sin x and X-axis from x = 0 to x = π: Area = ∫₀^π sin x dx = [−cos x]_0^π = 2 sq. units.
Area bounded by y = sin x from 0 to 2π: Area = |∫₀^π sin x dx| + |∫_π^(2π) sin x dx| = 2 + 2 = 4 sq. units.
Area bounded by y = |x| and horizontal line y = c: Forms a triangle with vertices (0, 0), (c, c), (−c, c). Area = ½ × base × height = ½(2c)(c) = c².
Area between y = sin x and y = cos x from x = 0 to x = π/4: Area = ∫₀^(π/4) (cos x − sin x) dx = [sin x + cos x]_0^(π/4) = √2 − 1.

formulas.label: sin x & cos x (0 to π/4)

nodes.title: Area Partitioning by Lines
points: Finding a line x = c that divides an area into two equal parts:
Step 1: Compute total area A between x = a and x = b.
Step 2: Set ∫_a^c f(x) dx = A / 2.
Step 3: Solve the resulting algebraic equation for c.
Classic Problem: Line x = a divides the area bounded by y² = 4x and x = 4 into two equal halves. Find a (Answer: a = 4^(2/3)).

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Questions
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive the area of circle x² + y² = a² using integration: Area = π a².
Board Favourite #2: Derive the area of ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 using integration: Area = π a b.
Board Favourite #3: Find the area bounded by the parabola y² = 4ax and its latus rectum x = a.
Board Favourite #4: Find the area enclosed between the parabola y² = 4x and the line y = 2x.
Board Favourite #5: Find the area of the region bounded by curves y² = 4ax and x² = 4ay.

nodes.title: MHT-CET 5-Second Area Shortcuts & Formulas
points: Master Shortcut #1: Parabola y² = 4ax and line y = mx ⟹ Area = (8/3)(a² / m³).
Master Shortcut #2: Parabola x² = 4by and line y = mx ⟹ Area = (8/3)(b² m³).
Master Shortcut #3: Two Parabolas y² = 4ax and x² = 4by ⟹ Area = (16/3) ab.
Master Shortcut #4: Parabola y² = 4ax and Latus Rectum x = a ⟹ Area = (8/3) a².
Master Shortcut #5: Ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 ⟹ Area = π a b.
Master Shortcut #6: Single sine/cosine arch (0 to π) ⟹ Area = 2 sq. units.
